name: Language Learning — English
intro: Global academic, professional and everyday communication. Build listening, speaking, reading and writing together using comprehensible input, deliberate output and spaced retrieval.
benchmark: CEFR progression + ACTFL-informed functional practice across listening, speaking, reading and writing. Use real communicative tasks and can-do evidence; this is not an official ACTFL rating.

ladder.title: Build sounds, core patterns and high-comprehension input

ladder.label: INTERMEDIATE – B1/B2
ladder.title: Sustain listening, conversation and reading in authentic contexts

ladder.label: ADVANCED – C1+
ladder.title: Use the language flexibly for complex, professional and cultural communication

video.title: English in a Minute box set

practiceBody: Record a 5-minute explanation, hold a 20-minute conversation, summarize an article and write a 500-word memo. Compare against a CEFR can-do rubric and ACTFL-informed functional lens, log recurring errors, create retrieval cards from those errors, and repeat after two weeks.
rubric: Comprehension at target difficulty; spontaneous interaction; intelligible pronunciation; vocabulary range; grammatical control; discourse length; reading inference; writing organization; ability to repair misunderstandings; documented improvement from feedback.

name: Programming Languages Mastery
intro: 2026 benchmark lens: GitHub Octoverse 2025 put TypeScript at #1 by contributor counts, followed by Python and JavaScript; Java and C# remained major enterprise languages. Stack Overflow 2025 also showed accelerating Python adoption and strong developer interest in Rust and Go. The pathway therefore teaches one primary stack deeply, then adds targeted secondary languages for transfer.
benchmark: GitHub Octoverse 2025 + Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 (current Sep 2026)

ladder.label: FOUNDATIONS
ladder.title: READ + REASON
ladder.body: Variables, types, control flow, functions, collections, debugging, Git, tests and command line.

ladder.label: INTERMEDIATE
ladder.title: BUILD APPLICATIONS
ladder.body: OOP / functional patterns, APIs, databases, async/concurrency, package ecosystems and secure input handling.

ladder.label: ADVANCED
ladder.title: ENGINEER SYSTEMS
ladder.body: Performance, architecture, observability, CI/CD, containers, profiling, reliability and idiomatic language design.

blocks.heading: Language Portfolio — Prioritize by Use Case (Do Not Learn All at Once)

items.title: TypeScript + JavaScript
items.body: Web/product default: browser, Node, React/Next, APIs, typed production code.

items.title: Python
items.body: AI/ML, data, automation, back-end services and rapid prototyping.

items.title: Java + C#
items.body: Enterprise systems, cloud services, large codebases, strong tooling and typed OOP.

items.title: SQL
items.body: Universal data fluency: querying, joins, modeling, transactions and performance.

items.title: Go + C++ + Rust
items.body: Cloud/platform, systems, performance, concurrency and safety tradeoffs.

items.title: Kotlin + Swift
items.body: Native mobile/application specialization after core programming mastery.

blocks.heading: Core Bootcamps
blocks.note: Long-form, hands-on learning bridges — code along, then rebuild without the video.

blocks.heading: Core Hands-On Session — 10-Day Build Camp
blocks.body: Days 1-2: syntax + debugging kata. Days 3-4: data structures + tests. Days 5-6: REST API + SQL. Day 7: authentication/error handling. Day 8: Git + CI. Day 9: containerize and instrument. Day 10: demo, code review, retrospective. Rule: after each code-along, close the video and rebuild the same behavior from a blank repository.

video.title: C++ Programming Course - Beginner to Advanced

items.title: Same Problem, Four Languages
items.body: Implement one validated JSON API in TypeScript, Python, Java/C# and Go. Compare error handling, types, testing, dependencies, throughput and developer friction.

items.title: Concurrency Lab
items.body: Build producer/consumer workers; instrument queue depth, throughput and failures; compare async/event-loop vs threads/goroutines/tasks.

items.title: Performance Lab
items.body: Profile a CPU- or memory-heavy workload. Optimize only after measurement; document changes and regressions.

items.title: Mobile Mini-Ship
items.body: Build a small native feature in Kotlin or Swift with local persistence, network call, loading/error states and accessibility checks.

practiceBody: Choose a primary language and ship three artifacts: CLI/data utility, API/service with persistence and tests, and a user-facing or distributed application. Then re-implement one bounded module in a second language and write a tradeoff memo comparing type system, concurrency, ecosystem, performance, testability and maintainability.
rubric: Readable, idiomatic code; tests that catch real failures; correct data/API contracts; secure input and secrets handling; debugging evidence; Git discipline; CI; measurable performance where relevant; clear tradeoffs; and the ability to modify the system under a new requirement without replaying the tutorial.

name: AI Mastery
tagline: Foundations → Build → Operate → Optimize, model-agnostic, eval-driven
intro: The Academy already contains AI courses; this pathway turns them into one end-to-end mastery route. The production benchmark emphasizes system scoping, grounding, tools/agents, evaluation, reliability, security, latency/cost and measurable task success — not prompt tricks alone.
benchmark: OpenAI Academy + Microsoft Learn AI Agent curricula (current Sep 2026)

ladder.label: FOUNDATIONS
ladder.title: UNDERSTAND
ladder.body: LLM behavior, tokens/context, prompting and context engineering, structured outputs, embeddings, model selection, limitations and responsible use.

ladder.label: BUILD
ladder.title: GROUND + ACT
ladder.body: RAG and retrieval quality, tool/function calling, agents, MCP, memory/state, workflow orchestration, human handoffs and product integration.

ladder.label: OPERATE
ladder.title: EVALUATE + RELY
ladder.body: Golden datasets, graders, regression gates, traces, prompt/model versioning, observability, prompt injection defenses, permissions, latency and cost.

blocks.heading: Production Bootcamp — System Scoping, Evals, Reliability, Safety, Cost, Adoption

video.title: How to Build Effective AI Agents

blocks.heading: 7-Day AI Builder Bootcamp
blocks.body: Day 1 – Scope: pick a costly real workflow; define user, task, baseline, non-goals, risks and measurable success. Day 2 – Ground: build retrieval with source metadata and a small relevance test set; inspect failure cases. Day 3 – Act: add one tool/API/MCP integration with explicit permissions, timeout, validation and fallback. Day 4 – Evaluate: create representative cases, rubrics/graders and regression thresholds for quality and safety. Day 5 – Operate: instrument traces, latency, token/cost and tool failures; add retries only where evidence supports them. Day 6 – Red Team: test injection, unsafe tool requests, data leakage, ambiguity and over-authority; tighten boundaries. Day 7 – Ship: stage rollout, human escalation, rollback/runbook, executive demo and measured adoption/task success.

practiceBody: Ship a production-style AI workflow with grounded context, at least one safe tool integration, an inspectable eval set, regression gates, traces, latency/cost metrics, explicit security/safety controls and a runbook. Defend when you would use prompt/context changes, RAG, fine-tuning, deterministic code or no AI at all.

name: UI & UX Mastery
tagline: Discover → Define → Design → Prototype → Test → Systematize → Measure
intro: The pathway separates UX research/problem understanding from UI craft while training the handoff between them. Core sequence uses long-form design instruction; short NN/g expert videos appear only as bonus micro-bridges when they add unique methodological value.
benchmark: Long-form design bootcamps + NN/g research (current Sep 2026)

ladder.label: FOUNDATIONS
ladder.title: DISCOVER + STRUCTURE
ladder.body: User/problem interviews, jobs/tasks, journey mapping, information architecture, interaction principles, accessibility basics and visual hierarchy.

ladder.label: INTERMEDIATE
ladder.title: DESIGN + PROTOTYPE
ladder.body: Wireframes, typography, color, spacing, grids, responsive design, components, auto-layout, prototypes, design critique and content design.

ladder.label: ADVANCED
ladder.title: TEST + SYSTEMATIZE
ladder.body: Usability testing, synthesis, experiment design, design systems/tokens, accessibility review, metrics, enterprise workflows and AI-assisted design with human judgment.

blocks.heading: Research & Design — Core Video / Bootcamp Bridges

video.title: Usability Testing with 5 Users: Design Process

blocks.heading: Hands-On Design Studio — 10-Session Product Design Bootcamp

items.title: 01 – Problem framing
items.body: Choose a real user workflow. Write assumptions, risks and research questions; avoid jumping to screens.

items.title: 02 – Interviews
items.body: Run 5 discovery interviews when appropriate; use open questions and record evidence, not conclusions.

items.title: 03 – Synthesis
items.body: Affinity map, jobs/tasks, journey and prioritized pain points. Separate quotes/observations from interpretations.

items.title: 04 – IA + flows
items.body: Create sitemap/navigation and task flows; test labels and states before high-fidelity polish.

items.title: 05 – Wireframe
items.body: Sketch multiple alternatives; critique against user task, constraints and error cases.

items.title: 06 – UI craft
items.body: Apply type, color, spacing, hierarchy, responsive layout and accessible contrast.

items.title: 07 – Components
items.body: Build reusable components/variants, auto-layout and starter design tokens.

items.title: 08 – Prototype
items.body: Create interactive happy path plus empty, loading, error, permission and recovery states.

items.title: 09 – Usability
items.body: Test representative tasks; note breakdowns, severity and evidence. Iterate the design.

items.title: 10 – Portfolio
items.body: Publish problem → evidence → decisions → prototype → testing → changes → outcome/next experiment.

practiceBody: Problem backed by user evidence; research ethics/consent; coherent IA and task flows; accessible visual craft; component consistency; realistic states; interactive prototype; usability evidence; iteration from observed failures; documented tradeoffs; outcome metric or test plan; and a concise case study that shows judgment rather than decorative screens.

name: Personal Development
tagline: Self-awareness, mindset, habits, focus, resilience, relationships, purpose
intro: Selection standard: evidence-informed ideas + high-reach speakers + practical transfer. TED and other widely followed voices are used because they can make difficult ideas memorable, but follower/view counts are never treated as proof that a claim is correct. Learners should test ideas against lived results and credible evidence.

items.title: 1. Self-Awareness + Values
items.body: Clarify values, strengths, recurring patterns, triggers and the gap between intended and actual behavior.

items.title: 2. Growth Mindset + Learning
items.body: Treat ability as developable where evidence supports it; seek feedback, productive difficulty and reflection.

items.title: 3. Habits + Self-Regulation
items.body: Shape cues, environment, friction, routines and accountability; measure behavior rather than motivation.

items.title: 4. Focus + Time
items.body: Prioritize, protect deep work, reduce distraction and understand procrastination patterns.

items.title: 5. Resilience + Stress Skills
items.body: Reappraise challenge, recover after setbacks, ask for support and build sustainable coping routines.

items.title: 6. Confidence + Courage
items.body: Practice honest self-expression, vulnerability with boundaries, assertiveness and exposure to meaningful discomfort.

items.title: 7. Relationships + Communication
items.body: Listen, repair, set boundaries, invest in high-quality relationships and practice empathy.

items.title: 8. Purpose + Life Design
items.body: Connect daily actions to meaning, contribution and long-term priorities; review tradeoffs intentionally.

blocks.heading: High-Reach Talks + Practice
blocks.note: TED-enriched, popular voices, reflection → experiment → behavior change.

video.title: Inside the Mind of a Master Procrastinator
How to Make Stress Your Friend
The Power of Believing You Can Improve
How to Stop Languishing and Start Finding Flow

practiceBody: Week 1: values/energy audit + one behavior baseline. Week 2: implement one habit with cue/friction design and daily tracking. Week 3: run five protected focus blocks and a digital-distraction audit. Week 4: invest deliberately in one relationship, practice one difficult conversation, and write a one-page life priorities review. Every week: retrieval-based reflection — what did I predict? What happened? What will I change?
rubric: Evidence of repeated practice, not inspirational consumption: baseline + target behavior; adherence data; an error/trigger log; at least two iterations; feedback from another person where appropriate; a short reflection distinguishing insight from measurable change; and one habit still running after 30 days.

name: Professional Development
tagline: Communication, influence, leadership, strategy, execution, business fluency, career capital, AI-era work
intro: Built for career-long transfer rather than a single job. The pathway combines executive communication, stakeholder influence, leadership, operating judgment, business fluency and visible proof of impact. Learners should adapt depth to level: individual contributor → manager → senior manager → director → executive.
benchmark: Stanford GSB + TED + Chicago Booth leadership/negotiation curricula (current Sep 2026)

items.title: 1. Communication + Executive Presence
items.body: Clear writing, spontaneous speaking, presentations, Q&A, listening and decision-ready synthesis.

items.title: 2. Storytelling + Data
items.body: Turn analysis into a narrative with evidence, implications, options and an explicit decision ask.

items.title: 3. Influence + Negotiation
items.body: Stakeholder mapping, interests, tradeoffs, conflict, persuasion, boundary setting and durable agreements.

items.title: 4. Leadership + Feedback
items.body: Direction, coaching, delegation, accountability, candor, recognition and difficult conversations.

items.title: 5. Team Effectiveness
items.body: Psychological safety, decision rights, operating norms, inclusion, conflict repair and high-quality meetings.

items.title: 6. Strategy + Decision Making
items.body: Diagnosis, choices, uncertainty, resource allocation, scenarios, pre-mortems and stop-doing decisions.

items.title: 7. Execution + Operating Rhythm
items.body: Goals, roadmap/program plan, dependencies, risks, KPI reviews, escalation and benefits realization.

items.title: 8. Career Capital + Network
items.body: Skill portfolio, sponsorship, reputation, networking, mentoring, interviewing and visible artifacts of impact.

blocks.heading: Masterclasses + Career Sprint
blocks.note: High-reach communication, leadership, negotiation, team practice.

video.title: Think Fast, Talk Smart: Communication Techniques
How to Speak So People Want to Listen
How to Lead With Radical Candor

practiceBody: Week 1 – Communicate: write a one-page executive memo and deliver a 5-minute briefing; record it and revise for clarity. Week 2 – Influence: build a stakeholder map and run a negotiation simulation; document interests, BATNA/tradeoffs and outcome. Week 3 – Lead: practice one coaching/feedback conversation and one delegation contract with observable expectations. Week 4 – Strategize: write a decision memo with diagnosis, options, economics, risks, recommendation and a stop-doing choice. Week 5 – Operate: create a KPI tree, review cadence, risk/dependency log and escalation mechanism for a real initiative. Week 6 – AI + Career Capital: automate or augment one workflow with AI and update your visible portfolio of impact.

name: Agent Mastery — Claude / Anthropic
tagline: Build from first principles with Claude agents and Claude Code, then connect external systems through MCP and harden the system for real work.
intro: Learn the shared agent architecture once, then build independently in Claude, Microsoft Copilot and Google Cloud/GCP — including tools, MCP servers/resources, memory, orchestration, evaluation, security, deployment and a working application/system.
benchmark: Official vendor agent-building documentation and workshops (current Sep 2026)

ladder.label: FOUNDATIONS
ladder.title: Understand the Agent Loop
ladder.body: Claude model behavior, instructions and context management; Claude Code agentic loop, project instructions and plan/act/observe; tools, resources, prompts, skills and sub-agents.

ladder.label: INTERMEDIATE
ladder.title: Connect + Orchestrate
ladder.body: MCP clients/servers, local and remote servers, resources and tool schemas; Agent Skills, tool discovery, code execution and multi-agent patterns; memory/state, retrieval, permissions and human approvals.

ladder.label: ADVANCED
ladder.title: Evaluate + Operate
ladder.body: Task suites, tool-use evals, tracing and regression gates; sandboxing, least privilege, prompt-injection defenses and containment; long-running/managed agents, reliability, cost and production rollout.

items.title: 01 – Agent shell
items.body: Install/configure Claude Code or Claude API/Agent SDK environment; define a real workflow, system prompt/project instructions and success criteria.

items.title: 02 – Knowledge + context
items.body: Add repository/files or retrieval context; establish explicit context boundaries and failure behavior.

items.title: 03 – Build an MCP server
items.body: Expose at least two typed tools and one useful resource; write precise descriptions, validation, auth and error handling.

items.title: 04 – Connect + act
items.body: Attach the MCP server; make Claude invoke tools on representative tasks; add one consequential write/action behind approval.

items.title: 05 – Skills + orchestration
items.body: Package one repeatable domain procedure as a Skill; optionally add sub-agents/parallel work where evidence supports it.

items.title: 06 – Evaluate + red team
items.body: Create representative tasks and assertions; test wrong-tool choice, injection, over-authority, secrets leakage and malformed tool responses.

items.title: 07 – Operate
items.body: Add logs/traces, retries/timeouts, cost/latency measures, sandbox/permission boundaries, runbook and rollback plan.

practiceBody: Build a functional Claude-powered operations or knowledge-work application that reads trusted context, discovers and calls your MCP tools, performs at least one real external action with human approval, uses a reusable Skill, passes a documented eval suite, records traces, handles tool failure safely and can be demonstrated end-to-end from user request to verified outcome.
rubric: Working behavior; correct MCP tool/resource discovery; schema quality; safe authentication; least privilege; meaningful approval boundaries; task-success evidence; adversarial testing; useful traces; failure recovery; latency/cost awareness; reproducible setup; and a concise architecture/decision record.

name: Agent Mastery — Microsoft Copilot
tagline: Build enterprise agents in Copilot Studio, extend them with knowledge, connectors, workflows and MCP, then publish with identity, evaluation, analytics and governance.
intro: Learn the shared agent architecture once, then build independently in Claude, Microsoft Copilot and Google Cloud/GCP — including tools, MCP servers/resources, memory, orchestration, evaluation, security, deployment and a working application/system.
benchmark: Official vendor agent-building documentation and workshops (current Sep 2026)

ladder.label: FOUNDATIONS
ladder.title: Build the Agent
ladder.body: Copilot Studio agent anatomy, instructions and generative orchestration; knowledge sources, connectors/tools and deterministic workflows; authentication, environments, testing and conversation tracing.

ladder.label: INTERMEDIATE
ladder.title: MCP + Enterprise Integration
ladder.body: Connect existing MCP servers; inspect tools/resources and selectively enable capabilities; create custom MCP servers with API key or OAuth 2.0 authentication; compose connected agents and integrate published Copilot Studio agents with Agent Framework.

ladder.label: ADVANCED
ladder.title: Publish + Govern
ladder.body: Evaluation test sets, quality measures and activity traces; Entra Agent ID, data policies, permissions, security and governance; publish to Teams/Microsoft 365/web; analytics, monitoring, adoption and cost controls.

items.title: 01 – Agent + scenario
items.body: Create a Copilot Studio agent for a real business workflow; define instructions, user groups, success measures and non-goals.

items.title: 02 – Ground + connect
items.body: Add approved knowledge and at least one connector/tool; separate knowledge lookups from actions.

items.title: 03 – MCP integration
items.body: Connect an MCP server or build one; inspect its tools/resources, disable irrelevant tools and configure authentication.

items.title: 04 – Workflow
items.body: Add a deterministic workflow/agent flow for one multi-step process and compare when workflow vs MCP vs connector is appropriate.

items.title: 05 – Identity + policy
items.body: Configure agent identity/authentication, least-privilege access and Power Platform data-policy boundaries.

items.title: 06 – Evaluate
items.body: Build a representative test set; inspect activity traces, tool arguments/results and failure paths; fix instructions/tool descriptions.

items.title: 07 – Publish + operate
items.body: Publish to an appropriate channel; configure monitoring/analytics, usage/cost awareness, change control and an incident/runbook path.

practiceBody: Build a functional Copilot Studio enterprise agent that answers from governed knowledge, calls an MCP tool, invokes a deterministic workflow, performs one permissioned action, authenticates correctly, passes a test set, exposes trace evidence and is published to a usable channel with analytics and governance controls.
rubric: Correct orchestration among knowledge, connectors, workflows and MCP; clean MCP descriptions/resources; identity and access correctness; traceable tool use; evaluation evidence; safe actions; policy compliance; usable channel experience; monitoring and operational ownership; cost awareness; and documented deployment/change controls.

name: Agent Mastery — Google Cloud / GCP
tagline: Build agents with Google ADK and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, connect governed MCP tools, compose multi-agent systems and deploy with IAM, evaluation and observability.
intro: Learn the shared agent architecture once, then build independently in Claude, Microsoft Copilot and Google Cloud/GCP — including tools, MCP servers/resources, memory, orchestration, evaluation, security, deployment and a working application/system.
benchmark: Official vendor agent-building documentation and workshops (current Sep 2026)

ladder.label: FOUNDATIONS
ladder.title: Build with ADK
ladder.body: ADK agents, instructions, tools, sessions/state and local development; workflow agents vs dynamic orchestration; multi-agent composition; Gemini models, retrieval/grounding and deployment choices.

ladder.label: INTERMEDIATE
ladder.title: MCP + Registry + A2A
ladder.body: Google Cloud remote MCP servers and custom MCP publishing; Agent Registry for agents, skills and MCP toolsets; dynamic discovery; A2A/remote agents, authentication and Agent Gateway policy mediation.

ladder.label: ADVANCED
ladder.title: Deploy + Govern
ladder.body: Agent Engine/Runtime, Cloud Run/GKE deployment and scaling; evaluation of task trajectories, tracing, latency, errors and token spend; IAM, VPC/service perimeters, content filtering, secrets, monitoring and cost controls.

items.title: 01 – ADK starter
items.body: Create a Python/TypeScript ADK agent with clear instructions, session/state handling and one local function tool.

items.title: 02 – Grounding + memory
items.body: Add approved enterprise/public context; define session memory behavior and source/uncertainty handling.

items.title: 03 – MCP
items.body: Connect a Google Cloud remote MCP server or publish/connect your own; authenticate and inspect tool schemas/behavior.

items.title: 04 – Registry + multi-agent
items.body: Register/discover an agent or MCP toolset; compose a parent orchestrator with a specialized remote/sub-agent using ADK/A2A patterns.

items.title: 05 – Security
items.body: Use IAM/service accounts/ADC, least privilege, secrets and gateway/policy controls; test denied and malformed requests.

items.title: 06 – Evaluate + observe
items.body: Create task/trajectory evals; inspect traces, latency, errors, token spend and tool-selection failures.

items.title: 07 – Deploy
items.body: Deploy through the appropriate managed runtime/Cloud Run/GKE path; add autoscaling, monitoring, release/rollback and cost guardrails.

practiceBody: Build a functional GCP agentic system with ADK that uses grounded context, calls a remote or custom MCP toolset, composes at least two specialized agents or one remote A2A agent, authenticates through IAM, passes trajectory/task evaluations, emits operational telemetry and is deployed to a cloud runtime with rollback and runbook evidence.
rubric: Working ADK architecture; correct session/state behavior; MCP tool discovery; registry/A2A composition; IAM correctness; least privilege; useful evals; diagnosable traces; reliable failure handling; deployability; latency/token/cost evidence; secure secret handling; production readiness and a clear architecture decision record.
